title: Compatibility and boundary tests for a legacy Rails stack
outcome: Plan a small change or upgrade using version-specific tests rather than broad rewrites.
useCase: Small legacy changes and planned runtime upgrades.
benefits: Confidence comes from relevant evidence rather than a total rewrite.
drawbacks: A compatibility matrix still has gaps outside tested seams.
cue: Record the version. Test the seam. Change one promise.

trace.title: Exact versions
trace.detail: Start by recording exact Ruby, Rails, gem, database, and frontend versions. A fork may differ from upstream. A copied snippet is a hypothesis until the relevant boundary test runs in an authorized isolated environment.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Choose one behavior → record current contract → write a failing/characterization test → make a small change → run affected boundary tests → verify deployment compatibility. Keep a matrix of versions only for the seams actually being changed.

Do not run course experiments inside the work checkout. Use synthetic data and a separately authorized test environment. Private source and data do not belong in the AI tutor.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: A full mock suite can hide broken autoload or SQL behavior. A modern Rails guide can use APIs absent in the old app. A test that merely copies implementation conditions adds little evidence.

recallPrompt: Without notes: Plan a small change or upgrade using version-specific tests rather than broad rewrites. Explain one example and one failure.
